title: Normalize subword-chain boundaries and role-escape handling for pinned-model onboarding and profile publish
creator: Asha Nair
description: When onboarding new model variants and publishing their performance profiles we observed mismatches between how our runtime normalizes subword chains (split/merge at punctuation and escapes) and how chat template rendering expects role delimiters. This can cause subtle token-count deltas, leading to pinned-version misbilling, incorrect KV cache keying, and evaluation regressions shown in profile diffs. This ticket is to design and implement a deterministic normalization pass that runs during onboarding/variant pinning and is published with the model's performance profile metadata so runtime and console agree on token counts and template placement.
reproduction_steps:
Pick model variant v2.1.3-internal and template 'assistant: {{content}}
---role: user---{{user}}'
Onboard model with default tokenizer shim and publish performance profile to runtime (runtime-1.22)
Run parity test: render chat templates with both the onboarding shim and the production runtime tokenizer and compare token counts and first-256 token prefix hashes
Observe differences for inputs containing partial punctuation (e.g., 'e-mail: alice@exam') and role-escape characters like '<<<' or '---'
observed_behavior: Token counts differ by 1-4 tokens for ~12% of samples in our onboarding corpus
KV cache keys computed at serving time don't match keys used in profile simulations, causing cache misses in canary rollouts
Performance profile publish shows inflated latency in tail percentiles due to extra tokens in some sequences
proposed_solution: Add a deterministic 'subword-chain normalization' pass to the onboarding pipeline that: lowercases where model-specific, collapses repeated escape sequences, and normalizes punctuation adjacency rules used by the runtime kernels
Expose the normalization version identifier in the model metadata (e.g., tokenizer_norm=v1) so pinned versions store the exact normalization used to generate profiles
Update profile publishing job to store both raw and normalized tokenization samples and include a token-diff histogram for quick console inspection
Add a lightweight runtime compatibility check that validates incoming requests' tokenization against the stored normalization and emits a warning metric (tokenization_mismatch) during canaries
tradeoffs_and_considerations: Tightening normalization rules may change upstream token counts used by customers if they re-onboard models — we will only apply for new pins and default to legacy for existing pinned versions
Storing extra normalized samples in profiles increases profile size; we will gzip and keep only top-N representative samples to bound storage
Runtime warning metric adds noise; we'll gate it behind canary and sampling to avoid alert storms
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): implement normalization pass in onboarding harness, unit tests, and offline profile generator (ETA 4 days)
Phase 2 (canary): onboard a non-critical model variant with normalization, publish profile to staging console, enable runtime compatibility check with sampling enabled (ETA 3 days)
Phase 3 (gradual rollout): after 72h of metrics stability, enable normalization for new pins and update console UI to show normalization ID next to profile (ETA 2 days)
Phase 4 (cleanup): propose migration guide for teams who want to re-pin existing variants under the new normalization (opt-in), and archive legacy-only profiles after 6 months
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests cover edge cases (emails, URLs, role-delimiters, repeated escapes)
Token-count parity: for a 1k-sample onboarding smoke set, normalized onboarding pass and runtime tokenization produce identical counts for >= 99.5% samples
Tokenization_mismatch metric shows <0.1% of production traffic in canary and falls to 0 after rollout
Performance profile publishing now includes 'token_diff_histogram' and 'tokenizer_norm' fields visible in staging console
